item.lead:
You now have encode and decode, so any string can become ids and back. Before that, the script must decide which part of the text the model may learn from.

A model is judged on text it has not studied, because a score on text it already learned would only show memory. So the one long string is cut in two: a large piece to learn from, a small piece held back. Look at the four lines that do it.

perform.line:
/explain Why is a language model checked on text it was not trained on, and how do these lines cut one string into a training piece and a held-back piece? Show it on the 1,115,394-character string: the first 90% (up to int(n*0.9)) trains, the rest from that same index validates.
The reader already knows: the character vocabulary, encode and decode, the string read from the file.
Do not cover: why validation text must stay unseen.
Afterwards the reader should be able to: state the cut and point at its lines.
